data.title: Largecap rally has more room to run after strongest earnings in two years: DSP MF
data.description:
The rally in largecap stocks is likely to sustain, driven by global fund reallocation and the strongest quarterly earnings print in two years, according to Vinit Sambre, Head of Equities at DSP Mutual Fund, which manages nearly $27 billion in assets.

Sambre highlighted that the July-September quarter of 2026 (Q2FY27) results demonstrated robust performance across major sectors, including banks and commodities. This marks a shift from the previous eight quarters, which were largely dominated by broader market gains.

"I think this has been the strongest print in the last eight quarters, and especially including the largecaps as well," he said in a chat with CNBC-TV18.

The recent underperformance in mid and smallcap stocks represents a typical asset reallocation phase rather than a cause for concern. Once largecap allocations build investor confidence in the broader economy, capital typically cascades down to smaller companies where growth metrics remain strong.

Foreign institutional flows are expected to follow this earnings trajectory, chasing asset classes that offer visible, high-growth metrics as long as corporate earnings do not falter.

Addressing corporate governance, particularly regarding portfolio holdings like APL Apollo Tubes, he said the focus remains strictly on minority shareholder interests. Markets, he noted, increasingly differentiate valuations based on governance standards, rewarding well-managed businesses with a premium while penalising those that prioritise short-term metrics.

"For the companies who want to sustain high valuations, who wants to look at wealth creation long term, it is very pertinent beyond businesses that the key stakeholders for their businesses needs to be brought in parity with their own," Sambre stated.

data.title: Dollar lingers near 22-month peak as AI worries simmer; kiwi rises
data.description:
Key points:
  • NZ dollar rises as election result reduces political uncertainty
  • Risk-sensitive Aussie buoyed as Asian stock gains lift sentiment
  • Dollar garners support from expectations for Fed rate hikes

The US dollar hovered below a 22-month peak in holiday-thinned trading on Friday, with traders looking to equity markets for clues on direction as doubts about the AI trade trigger heightened volatility.

The New Zealand dollar rose after long-awaited results of the general election reduced political uncertainty, even with no clear winner. The Aussie dollar was also pulled higher by its neighbour.

The dollar index , which measures the currency against a basket of six peers, was steady at 103.74, at the end of a week that saw it pop to the highest level since March of last year at 104.53 on Monday only to erase those gains a day later. For the week, the index is currently down 0.1%.

The US currency was steady at 159.27 yen midway into Friday's Asian session, and has been pinned below 160 yen by worries of another round of Japanese intervention.

The greenback weakened 0.1% to 0.83435 Swiss franc .

The euro was little changed at $1.09725 and sterling gained slightly to $1.3118.

"All eyes are on whether the downtrend in AI-related stocks will turn around," Mizuho analysts wrote in a client note.

A recovery could see currencies such as the Aussie and high-yielding Mexican peso bounce back, while renewed selling would likely see those currencies under additional pressure, they said.

Japan's tech-heavy Nikkei share index gained 2% on Friday, while South Korea's KOSPI climbed 3.9%.

The risk-sensitive Aussie dollar added 0.4% to $0.66635, finding its feet after dipping to a one-year low of $0.6559 on Wednesday.

It also got support from a jump in the kiwi dollar earlier in the session, as results of the general election initially lifted the local currency as much as 0.6%. However, those gains later ebbed, and the currency was last 0.3% higher on the day at $0.5484.

New Zealand Prime Minister Christopher Luxon will seek the support of the centrist Opportunity Party to keep his ruling centre-right coalition in power after official results on Friday showed he fell just short of a parliamentary majority.

"NZD has risen slightly on the reduction — but not removal — of uncertainty, but the move is polluted by the USD effect," said Imre Speizer, Westpac's head of New Zealand market strategy.

"Risks of another breakdown remain, and we wouldn't rule out $0.5400 during the week ahead," he said. "Much of the bearish impetus has been due to the surging US dollar and hawkish Fed repricing."

The US currency has been supported by expectations for Federal Reserve policy tightening, with traders seeing a quarter-point interest rate hike on December 9 as a near certainty, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool.

Hotter-than-expected US core personal consumption expenditures inflation in October, a sharp upward revision to third-quarter gross domestic product and a Federal Reserve survey showing continued economic growth and sticky inflation also have traders confident of an additional hike by around April.

The dollar index has risen about 5.7% so far in 2026, with only a month left in the year. The index is up 1.7% this month, putting it on track for its first run of three straight monthly gains since the final three months of 2024.

"The USD looks to be on a stronger-for-longer path than previously expected," NAB strategists wrote in a research report.

However, "given its rapid rise, we see limited scope for further gains," they added.

data.title: SG Mart, E2E Networks will not be included in the latest MSCI inclusion - Here's the reason why
data.description:
Global index provider MSCI has halted the inclusion of two Indian small-cap stocks, namely SG Mart and E2E Networks, ahead of their November 2026 index review, scheduled for implementation after market close on Monday, November 30, 2026, and effective from December 1.

Both companies had previously been identified as potential additions to the MSCI Global Small Cap Indexes. However, MSCI confirmed that neither stock will be added during this review cycle after both were placed on the Ineligible Alert Board due to domestic regulatory surveillance.

Why Will SG Mart, E2E Not Be Included?

Under Appendix I of the MSCI Global Investable Market Indexes (GIMI) Methodology, securities placed under India’s Short-Term or Long-Term Additional Surveillance Measures (ASM) framework are automatically disqualified from index additions during reviews.

Both the stocks are currently under Stage 1 of the Long-term ASM Framework.

Because inclusion in an MSCI index typically triggers substantial passive inflows from global exchange-traded funds (ETFs) and institutional trackers, missing the cut deprives both stocks of anticipated institutional liquidity.

SG Mart’s sudden placement under exchange surveillance and subsequent MSCI exclusion follows severe market turbulence across companies promoted by the Sanjay Gupta-led family, the founding group behind both SG Mart and APL Apollo Tubes.

Investors and proxy advisory firms (such as IiAS) raised sharp concerns over the deal's structure and valuation—specifically noting that Tata Steel Colors was being sold to APL Apollo at ₹16,300 crore, more than seven times its implied ₹2,200 crore valuation from late 2025.

The sell-off spilled directly into promoter-linked group entities. Coupled with SG Mart's own board meeting announcements regarding fundraising plans, SG Mart shares plunged—hitting a 20% lower circuit on November 25 before staging a partial rebound.

What Is The ASM Framework?

Introduced jointly by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) and domestic stock exchanges (NSE and BSE), the Additional Surveillance Measure (ASM) framework is designed to curb excessive speculation and alert investors to unusual trading activity.

For both SG Mart and E2E Networks, eligibility for MSCI index inclusion will now remain on hold until they exit the ASM framework and qualify again in a subsequent quarterly review.

Shares of SG Mart are trading 4% higher on Friday at ₹916.25. The stock is still up 140% so far this year.

data.title: India's PNB brings in Deutsche Bank as state lenders move into takeover finance
data.description:
IntelliNews summary:

  • The PNB-Deutsche Bank memorandum is a non-binding framework covering underwriting, syndication and referrals; no deal or amount has been named.
  • RBI rules in force since July 1 let banks lend up to 75% of a deal's value, up from 70% in the October 2025 draft.
  • A bank's acquisition-finance exposure is capped at 20% of its eligible capital base, double the draft's 10% of Tier 1 capital.
  • Foreign-owned and controlled companies in India cannot use the domestic bank route.

____________________

India's Punjab National Bank has signed up Deutsche Bank to help fund corporate takeovers, becoming the third state lender this year to announce a tie-up with a foreign bank as domestic lenders enter acquisition finance.

The memorandum of understanding, disclosed to the stock exchanges after trading closed on November 25, gives the two banks a framework to underwrite, arrange, join, syndicate or refer acquisition-finance deals for clients in India, with each bank's role set deal by deal. It names no borrower, target or amount, commits neither side to any transaction and leaves each to take its own credit decisions, Business Today reported.

State Bank of India signed a strategic partnership with Japan's MUFG Bank in March, and Bank of Baroda followed with Mizuho Bank on June 30, agreeing to originate, structure, co-underwrite and syndicate takeover loans together. Three of the largest public-sector banks have now each recruited a foreign house as Indian banks enter a business they were previously not permitted to finance directly.

What banks may lend

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) issued its final rules in February, then deferred them to July 1 after banks and industry groups asked for more time, clarifying several points in a revised version on March 30. Under the revised directions, a bank may lend up to 75% of the acquisition value as assessed by its own independent valuers. The acquirer must put up the rest from internal accruals, asset sales or fresh equity, and borrowed money does not count.

The borrower must be an Indian non-financial company with a net worth of at least INR5bn ($53.9mn) and three straight years of net profit, plus an investment-grade rating if it is unlisted. The deal has to deliver control of a target that is not a related party, and the buyer's consolidated debt may not exceed three times its equity afterwards. A bank's total acquisition-finance book is capped at 20% of its eligible capital base, inside a 40% ceiling on all capital-market exposure, according to the concentration-risk rules.

The October 2025 draft was tighter on each of the headline limits, offering 70% of deal value, requiring 30% from the buyer and limiting each bank's exposure to 10% of its Tier 1 capital.

Key RBI acquisition-finance limits, October 2025 draft v final directions in force from July 1, 2026. Exposure cap measured against Tier 1 capital in the draft and the eligible capital base in the final rules. Source: Reserve Bank of India. IntelliNews

Fees for the foreign partner

Until this year, Indian acquirers relied on non-bank lenders, private credit and offshore banks to borrow for takeovers, according to the India chapter of the Chambers Banking & Finance 2026 guide, written by AZB & Partners. In each pairing the Indian bank supplies the lending capacity and the domestic relationships, while the foreign partner supplies syndication desks and a record of underwriting debt-funded takeovers. The rules also let overseas branches of Indian banks join offshore syndicates outside the chapter's limits, provided a single bank funds no more than 20% of the deal.

'The acquisition finance market is a very, very big market and ample opportunities are there in the system,' PNB Managing Director Ashok Chandra told PTI in July, adding that the bank was 'looking for a good partner' and could start in the October-December quarter, beginning with domestic deals.

The tie-up sits in the part of Deutsche Bank's Indian business that it chose to keep. In June it agreed to sell its Indian retail, private banking and wealth arms to Kotak Mahindra Bank while retaining its corporate and investment bank there. 'India's growing integration into the global economy reinforces its position as a core market for Deutsche Bank,' Kaushik Shaparia, chief executive of Deutsche Bank Group India and Emerging Asia, said at the time.

Not open to everyone

Foreign-owned and controlled companies in India cannot use domestic bank acquisition finance, because foreign-exchange rules bar them from borrowing locally for such investments, according to the Chambers guide. That shuts out the Indian subsidiaries of multinationals and leaves the bank route to Indian-owned groups.

Bank lending was already winning business from the bond market before the rules took effect. Crisil Ratings said in April that corporates preferred bank credit because bond yields had moved above banks' lending rates, and named acquisition financing among the new avenues likely to support loan growth. Takeover loans give the state banks a new corporate product at a time when foreign capital is flowing into Indian finance itself, from Emirates NBD's majority stake in RBL Bank to the approved sale of 60.72% of IDBI Bank to a Fairfax unit. The risk the RBI has accepted is concentration in a handful of large state balance sheets, which it has bounded with the 20% exposure cap, the 3:1 debt ceiling and a mandatory pledge of the acquired shares.

data.title: Is this a dead turkey bounce?
data.description:
A look at the day ahead in European and global markets from Stella Qiu

With Wall Street off for Thanksgiving, Asian shares found some holiday cheer, bouncing back after a bruising month when investors' faith in the AI trade was badly shaken by the shock departure and return of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.

Nasdaq futures rallied 2.4% while S&P 500 futures gained 1.6%. European shares looked set to extend the rally, with pan-region stock futures up 0.6%.

Japan's Nikkei jumped 1.9% to bring its gains for the week to 3.8%, clawing back some of its 7.4% loss for the month. South Korea jumped 3.9%, while Chinese blue chips also bounced 0.2%, having hit the lowest level since June 2025 just a day earlier.

Whether the rebound has legs or is simply a dead cat bounce in thin holiday liquidity is the trillion-dollar question. The king of the AI trade may be back, but that hardly guarantees a return to the days of easy money for the wider AI ecosystem. Nvidia has reportedly halted server sales to four Southeast Asian countries.

And it is not just the flow of chips that is coming under greater scrutiny, but the flow of money underpinning the AI boom. The Bank of England warned on Thursday that increasingly complex, circular and opaque AI financing arrangements raised the risk of financial contagion.

Still, the risk rally saved the beleaguered Antipodean currencies and pushed Treasury yields a little higher. The kiwi got a little boost from the final election count that left the ruling centre-right coalition just one seat shy of a majority.

Gold rallied 1.8% while silver surged 4.8%, though much hinges on whether the revival in risk appetite lasts. King dollar, meanwhile, is still on a roll, charging towards a third straight month of gains even as bets on a half-point Fed hike fade.

Key developments that could influence markets on Friday:

-- French CPI for November

-- Euro zone consumer confidence for November

data.title: Euro Zone picks Spain's Pablo Hernandez de Cos as next ECB president
data.description:
• Spanish central banking veteran Pablo Hernández de Cos was selected by euro zone countries on Thursday to succeed Christine Lagarde as president of the European Central Bank.
  • The mandate for the President of the European Central Bank is for 8 years and non-renewable.
  • At the same time, the European Council put forward Laurence Boone and Markus Brunnermeier as members of the ECB’s executive board, replacing current members Isabel Schnabel and Philip Lane. Schnabel announced her intention to step down from her position on January 3, 2027. Lane’s term ends on May 31, 2027.
  • The European Council will now consult the European Parliament and the ECB's governing council on all three candidatures before taking a formal decision, it said in a statement.
  • Reuters reported that de Cos was set for the nomination after the Netherlands agreed to back Klaas Knot, the only other candidate, citing European diplomatic sources.
  • de Cos, the 55-year-old economist and career central banker, built his career at the Bank of Spain, joining as a researcher in the 1990s before rising through various roles to become governor from 2018 to June 2024. He also chaired the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision from 2019 to 2024 and has served as general manager of the Bank for International Settlements in Basel since July 2025.

data.title: Japan’s crypto security group taps SEAL to speed up hack response
data.description:
Japan’s crypto industry cybersecurity group has signed an agreement with US nonprofit Security Alliance (SEAL) to improve the detection of cyberattacks and respond to incidents more effectively.

According to a statement released Friday, the memorandum will see JPCrypto-ISAC receive help from SEAL to develop an incident response support framework and give them access to SEAL’s incident response and support capabilities. Both organizations will also share cyber threat intelligence.

In the Web3 and digital asset sector, addressing cyber threats that transcend national borders has become essential, said JPCrypto-ISAC representative director Naoji Noda. “We are delighted to establish this partnership with SEAL through this MOU.”

JPCrypto-ISAC had 16 full members at launch in 2025, including SBI VC Trade, bitbank, GMO Coin and Rakuten Wallet. The organization helps Japanese crypto companies share and analyze cyber threat intelligence.

Earlier this month, Japanese crypto exchanges Zaif and CoinTrade disclosed that a breach at their email provider, Arara, exposed hundreds of thousands of customer email addresses.

Arara estimated that the breach may have affected up to 380 companies across its customer base.

Japan’s crypto industry suffered a major breach in May 2024, when hackers stole Bitcoin worth about $305 million at the time from crypto exchange DMM Bitcoin. US and Japanese authorities later attributed the theft to North Korean hackers.

data.title: Nifty IT index could hit new high in 12-18 months as AI demand picks up: Sowilo Investment
data.description:
Stronger technology spending, improving earnings and recovering demand could help the Nifty IT index scale a new high over the next 12 to 18 months, according to Sandip Agarwal, Fund Manager at Sowilo Investment Managers.

He expects Indian IT stocks to outperform as enterprises step up artificial intelligence (AI) deployments across industries.

He believes domestic software exporters are well placed to capture a large share of AI implementation work because of their dominant position in the global outsourcing market. As enterprise spending gathers pace, he expects demand and profitability to improve across the sector.

Agarwal said enterprises have begun moving from AI experimentation to wider deployment, creating fresh opportunities for technology service providers.

"We firmly believe that when enterprise AI adoption increases, Indian IT services companies are the only ones who can service that and who will get the market share there," he said.

He expects the sector to deliver 45-70% cumulative EPS growth over the next two to three years, driven by stronger demand, margin expansion and currency support. According to him, consensus estimates do not fully reflect the earnings potential, with many companies capable of reporting around 20% EPS growth next year.

Agarwal said the recent appreciation in the rupee may weigh on quarterly numbers, but the impact is likely to be temporary because most IT companies use rolling hedging strategies.

Another indicator supporting his positive outlook is the pickup in employee attrition. Agarwal said higher attrition has historically coincided with improving demand for technology services.

"I think the attrition rates are again picking up in the sector, which is a very positive sign. It is a clear sign that we will see very good growth going forward," he said.

He added that several largecap IT stocks have lagged despite improving fundamentals and could participate in the sector's next leg of gains as AI-led technology spending continues to increase.

data.title: InnoCare Announces Approval of the Next-Generation TRK Inhibitor Zurletrectinib for the Treatment of Pediatric Patients with Solid Tumors in China
data.description:
BEIJING, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- InnoCare Pharma HKEX:09969, a leading biopharmaceutical company focusing on the treatment of cancer and autoimmune diseases, announced today that its next-generation TRK inhibitor, zurletrectinib (ICP-723), has received approval from the China National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) for the treatment of pediatric patients (aged 2 to 12) with solid tumors harboring NTRK gene fusions.

In December 2025, zurletrectinib received approval for the treatment of adult and adolescent patients (aged 12 years and older) with solid tumors harboring NTRK gene fusions in China.

In the registrational clinical trial for pediatric patients with NTRK fusion-positive solid tumors, zurletrectinib demonstrated outstanding efficacy and a favorable safety profile. As assessed by the Independent Review Committee (IRC), both the objective response rate (ORR) and the disease control rate (DCR) were 100%, and the 24-month duration of response (DOR) rate was 74.1%.

As a next-generation TRK inhibitor, zurletrectinib demonstrated superior efficacy compared to first-generation TRK inhibitors in the treatment of both adult and pediatric patients with solid tumors. It delivered durable deep remissions and exhibits strong brain penetration activity with a good safety profile. Moreover, it has also been shown to overcome acquired resistance to first-generation TRK inhibitors. The once-daily oral dosing offers great convenience to patients. Notably, the orally disintegrating tablet (ODT) formulation developed for pediatric patients disintegrates quickly in saliva and requires little or no water for administration, greatly improving medication adherence in pediatric patients.

Dr. Jasmine Cui, the co-founder, chairwoman, and CEO of InnoCare, said, “We would like to thank all the physicians and patients who participated in this study, as well as our partners for their strong support and our employees for their unremitting efforts. InnoCare has been dedicated to developing therapies that are differentiated in mechanism of action, efficacy, and safety. We expect to see zurletrectinib benefit more solid tumor patients.”

NTRK gene fusion is a driving factor in various adult and pediatric cancers. In some rare tumors, such as infantile fibrosarcoma, salivary gland carcinoma, and secretory breast cancer, the incidence of NTRK gene fusion exceeds 90%. It is estimated that about 6,500 new cases of NTRK fusion-positive solid tumors diagnosed in China each year. Patients have long faced a scarcity of effective therapeutic agents, representing significant unmet clinical need.

About InnoCare Pharma

InnoCare (SSE: 688428; HKEX: 09969) is a commercial stage biopharmaceutical company committed to discovering, developing, and commercializing innovative drugs for the treatment of cancers and autoimmune diseases, two therapeutic areas with unmet medical needs worldwide. InnoCare has established comprehensive innovation platforms for drug discovery. To date, the Company has developed a robust product pipeline comprising three approved drugs (orelabrutinib, tafasitamab and zurletrectinib), more than ten innovative drug candidates in clinical development, and multiple programs in preclinical stages. InnoCare has branches in Beijing, Nanjing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, Hong Kong, and the United States.
